SMTO-SKL-0187 — SMTO couldn't find the file to upload to GitHub

GUID: 58e0e3b8-949c-5620-a91f-c71a3a87b3b1
Slug: github-artifact-reference-invalid
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: github

What happened

  • The Agent tried to upload a file to GitHub, but SMTO couldn't find that file among this Conversation's files, or couldn't open it. SMTO only uploads files that belong to the current Conversation. Nothing was uploaded.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Attach the file using the Add context button next to the message box, then Add files to conversation. SMTO only uploads files that belong to this Conversation, not files from other places on the computer.
  2. If the file is on a computer connected through a Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses to work on other computers), first ask the Agent to bring that file into this Conversation. Files on a Gateway computer must be copied into the Conversation before they can go to GitHub.
  3. Ask the Agent to upload the file again, naming the attached file. Nothing was uploaded this time, so trying again with the right file is safe.

What success looks like

  • The file appears in the release's Assets list on github.com.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, with the name of the file you attached.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The release asset upload's source_ref is not an artifact://, art_ or artifact-workspace:// reference, or resolving/opening it in the conversation's ArtifactStore raised ValueError or OSError (unknown, not owned by this conversation, or unreadable).

What this means

  • Upload artifact resolution raises ValueError or OSError for the selected source. This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.

Why this can happen

  • Upload artifact resolution raises ValueError or OSError for the selected source.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect reference scheme, scope and source materialization without using arbitrary host paths.

How to fix it

  • Pass a conversation-owned source: artifact://ID, art_ID, or an artifact-workspace:// URI from this run; local Server paths are never accepted. Stage files that live on a Gateway through the existing Artifact/File transfer first, then confirm the artifact opens for this conversation_id before uploading.
  • Select a conversation-owned artifact:// or artifact-workspace:// source. Stage Gateway files through existing Artifact/File transfer first.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The exact supported artifact resolves and passes integrity checks.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
